title: 2023 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）

sections.title: Section I　完形填空
sections.dir: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 主线：小企业靠“增长团队”突破增长瓶颈。7 题看 despite 让步，11 题 lack 与后文 unaware 呼应。

paras.en: Here's a common scenario that any number of entrepreneurs face today: you're the CEO of a small business, and though you're making a nice 1 , you need to find a way to take it to the next level. What you need to do is 2 growth by establishing a growth team. A growth team is made up of members from different departments within your company, and it harnesses the power of collaboration to focus 3 on finding ways to grow.
paras.zh: 任何一位企业家今天都可能遇到这样一种常见情形：你是一家小企业的首席执行官，尽管眼下 1 不错，你还是得想办法让它更上一层楼。你需要做的是，通过组建增长团队来 2 增长。增长团队由公司内部不同部门的成员组成，它借助协作的力量，让团队 3 专注于寻找增长的办法。

paras.en: Let's look at a real-world 4 . Prior to forming a growth team, the software company BitTorrent had 50 employees working in the 5 departments of engineering, marketing and product development. This brought them good results until 2012, when their growth plateaued. The 6 was that too many customers were using the basic, free version of their product. And 7 improvements to the premium, paid version, few people were making the upgrade.
paras.zh: 我们来看一个现实中的 4 。在组建增长团队之前，软件公司 BitTorrent 有 50 名员工，分别在工程、营销和产品开发这些 5 部门工作。这种配置给他们带来了不错的业绩，直到 2012 年增长陷入停滞。6 在于太多客户使用的都是产品的基础免费版本。而且 7 付费的高级版本做了种种改进，升级的人依然很少。

paras.en: Things changed, 8 , when an innovative project-marketing manager came aboard, 9 a growth team and sparked the kind of 10 perspective they needed. By looking at engineering issues from a marketing point of view, it became clear that the 11 of upgrades wasn't due to a quality issue. Most customers were simply unaware of the premium version and what it offered. Armed with this 12 , the marketing and engineering teams joined forces to raise awareness by prominently 13 the premium version to users of the free version. 14 , upgrades skyrocketed, and revenue increased by 92 percent.
paras.zh: 情况发生了改变，8 ，一位富有创新精神的项目营销经理加入公司，9 了一个增长团队，并激发出他们所需的那种 10 视角。从营销的角度审视工程问题后，可以清楚地看到，升级人数 11 并不是因为质量问题。大多数客户只是根本不知道有高级版本，也不知道它能提供什么。掌握了这一 12 之后，营销与工程团队联手，通过向免费版用户重点 13 高级版本，来提升他们的认知。14 ，升级量猛增，收入增长了 92%。

paras.en: But in order for your growth team to succeed, it needs to have a strong leader. It needs someone who can 15 the interdisciplinary team and keep them on course for improvement. This leader will 16 the target area, set clear goals and establish a time frame for the 17 of these goals. The growth leader is also 18 for keeping the team focused on moving forward and steering them clear of distractions. 19 attractive new ideas can be distracting, the team leader must recognize when these ideas don't 20 the current goal and need to be put on the back burner.
paras.zh: 但要让你的增长团队取得成功，它需要有一位强有力的领导者。这个人要能把跨学科团队 15 起来，并让他们始终朝着改进的方向前进。这位领导者要 16 目标领域，设定清晰的目标，并为这些目标的 17 确定时间表。增长团队的领导者还 18 让团队专注于向前推进，并引导他们避开各种干扰。19 有吸引力的新想法会让人分心，团队领导者必须识别出这些想法何时不再 20 当前目标，从而需要暂时搁置。

items.exp: 定位首段 you're making a nice ___ , you need to find a way to take it to the next level。take it to the next level 指“更上一层楼”，前提是眼下已经赚到了钱，故 profit（收益）。purchase（采购）、connection（人脉）与“做大生意”这一目标接不上；bet 是本段末 growth team 那套“押注”口吻的干扰，但 make a nice bet 不能说成“目前状况不错”。

定位 What you need to do is ___ growth by establishing a growth team。后文整篇都在讲“把增长放在第一位、组建团队去攻”，故 prioritize（优先处理）。define 与 predict 都只停在“界定/预测”，不能落到“成立团队去做”；appreciate 意为“意识到、感激”，与 by establishing 的手段关系不搭。

定位 it harnesses the power of collaboration to focus ___ on finding ways to grow。团队的价值就在于把各部门力量集中到“找增长办法”这一件事上，focus exclusively on 即“只专注于”，故 A。temporarily（暂时）与 initially（起初）都把这种专注说成临时的，削弱了“团队”的意义；potentially（潜在地）是可能性副词，不能修饰 focus on 这种实指动作。
定位 Let's look at a real-world ___ .。后文紧接着讲 BitTorrent 这家公司的具体经历，是拿它当“实例”来印证上段的道理，故 example。experiment 指人为设计的实验，BitTorrent 并非受控实验；proposal（提案）、debate（争论）与下文叙事都对不上。

定位 50 employees working in the ___ departments of engineering, marketing and product development。工程、营销、产品开发是公司里原本就有的“老部门”，与后文新设的 growth team 相对，故 traditional。identical（完全相同的）会被误读成“各部门一模一样”；marginal（边缘的）、provisional（临时的）都贬低了这三个核心部门。

定位 The ___ was that too many customers were using the basic, free version of their product。前一句说 growth plateaued（增长停滞），此处解释停滞的根源，故 problem。rumor（传闻）、myth（讹传）都暗示“说法不实”，而“多数人只用免费版”是事实；secret（秘密）与后文公开分析的口吻不符。
定位 And ___ improvements to the premium, paid version, few people were making the upgrade。前半是“付费版有不少改进”，后半是“升级的人很少”，前后相反，需要让步介词，故 despite。through 会变成“因为改进所以少人升级”，因果颠倒；besides 是递加，unlike 是比较，都无法承载这层转折。
定位 Things changed, ___ , when an innovative project-marketing manager came aboard。上一段讲的是增长停滞、升级者寥寥，本段转入转机，前后相反，故 however。moreover 表递加、therefore 表因果，都会把“转机”说成上一段困境的延续或结果；again 表重复，文中并无“又一次”之意。

定位 came aboard, ___ a growth team and sparked the kind of ___ perspective they needed。这位经理新来乍到，与 a growth team 搭配的动作只能是“组建”，故 created。inspected（检查）、reformed（改造）都预设团队已经存在；expanded（扩大）同样需要原有基础，与“新官上任后才有团队”矛盾。
定位 sparked the kind of ___ perspective they needed。下文说他“从营销角度看工程问题”，这是公司里此前没有的视角，故 fresh（新鲜的、新的）。cultural（文化的）与视角搭配生硬；objective（客观的）暗示此前不客观，文中无此对比；personal（个人的）会把“跨部门视角”缩小成“私人看法”。

定位 it became clear that the ___ of upgrades wasn't due to a quality issue。后一句给出真正原因——客户根本不知道有高级版，可见问题是“升级的人太少”，即 the lack of upgrades。end of upgrades 意为“升级终止”，与“仍有人在升级、只是少”不符；burden（负担）与 decrease 都不能与 of upgrades 组成“升级不足”这一含义，decrease 还多一层“正在下降”的动态。
定位 Armed with this ___ , the marketing and engineering teams joined forces。空指代上文刚刚“看清”的结论——不是质量问题，而是客户不知情，这是一份“洞见”，故 insight。policy（政策）需由管理层制定，两个团队无此权限；suggestion 是向别人提的建议，purpose 是目的，都不能指“查明真相后的认识”。

定位 raise awareness by prominently ___ the premium version to users of the free version。手段是“让免费版用户知道高级版”，即向用户“推介”，故 promoting。transferring（转移）会把句子变成“把高级版转给用户”，主体成了版本流转，不是提升认知；allocating（分配）的对象是资源、名额，不能是“版本”；contributing 需接 to，且意为“贡献”，与 by 搭配不通。
定位 ___ , upgrades skyrocketed, and revenue increased by 92 percent。前文是“向免费用户推介高级版”，此处是结果——升级量猛增、收入涨 92%，故 As a result。At any rate（无论如何）表退让，By the way（顺便说）表话题转换，In a sense（在某种意义上）表限定，三者都承担不了因果收束。

定位 It needs someone who can ___ the interdisciplinary team and keep them on course。领导者对跨学科团队的作用是“把不同部门的人拢到一起”，故 unite。follow（跟随）把领导变成追随者，与 keep them on course 的带队语气正相反；finance（为……出资）说的是钱，choose（挑选）只涉及选人，都不是“带领”。
定位 This leader will ___ the target area, set clear goals。先“锁定”目标领域，才谈得上设定清晰目标，故 identify。divide（划分）会把“锁定目标”变成“拆分目标”，与 set clear goals 层次混乱；broaden（拓宽）则是扩大范围，与“设定明确目标”方向相反；share（分享）缺宾语对象，最弱。
定位 establish a time frame for the ___ of these goals。为“目标的达成”定时间表，故 accomplishment。assessment（评估）最易误选——目标确实要评估，但时间表对的是“做完”，不是“打分”；announcement（宣布）、adjustment（调整）虽都能接 of these goals，同样不需要预设期限。

定位 The growth leader is also ___ for keeping the team focused。be responsible for doing 是固定搭配，意为“负责做某事”，故 responsible。famous for 意为“因……出名”，available for 意为“可供……使用”，respectable（体面的）根本不接 for + 动名词，三者都无法表达职责。

定位 ___ attractive new ideas can be distracting, the team leader must recognize when...。前半承认“新想法确实会让人分心”，后半说“领导必须判断何时该搁置”，两句是让步对照，故 While（虽然）。Once 表“一旦”，会把“分心”变成条件；Unless 反转逻辑（除非会分心才要判断）；Before 只表时间先后，说不通。

定位 the team leader must recognize when these ideas don't ___ the current goal and need to be put on the back burner。serve the goal 意为“服务于该目标”，与“该搁置”构成因果：不服务于目标，才要放一放，故 serve。alter（改变）看似可接 goal，但“没改变目标”并不是搁置一个想法的理由；limit（限制）、summarize（概括）与“有用与否”这层判断无关。

sections.title: Text 1　人造草坪之争
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：RHS 禁展、请愿征税，业界反辩真草也有代价。24 题政府“不立法、只要求守规”最易读成立法。

paras.en: In the quest for the perfect lawn, homeowners across the country are taking a shortcut—and it is the environment that is paying the price. About eight million square metres of plastic grass is sold each year but opposition has now spread to the highest gardening circles. The Chelsea Flower Show has banned fake grass from this year's event, declaring it to be not part of its ethos. The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS), which runs the annual show in west London, says it has introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity.
paras.zh: 为了追求完美的草坪，全国家庭都在走捷径——而付出代价的是环境。每年售出约八百万平方米的塑料草坪，但反对的声音如今已传到园艺界的最高层。切尔西花展已禁止人造草坪参加今年的展会，宣称它不符合自己的理念。每年在伦敦西部举办该展会的皇家园艺学会（RHS）表示，之所以出台禁令，是因为塑料草坪会对环境和生物多样性造成破坏。

paras.en: Ed Horne, of the RHS, said: “We launched our sustainability strategy last year and fake grass is just not in line with our ethos and views on plastic. We recommend using real grass because of its environmental benefits, which include supporting wildlife, alleviating flooding and cooling the environment.”
paras.zh: 皇家园艺学会的埃德·霍恩说：“我们去年启动了可持续发展战略，人造草坪与我们的理念以及我们对塑料的看法完全不符。我们建议使用真草，因为它有环境上的好处，包括为野生动植物提供支持、缓解洪水以及给环境降温。”

paras.en: The RHS's decision comes as campaigners try to raise awareness of the problems fake grass causes. A Twitter account, which claims to “cut through the greenwash” of artificial grass, already has more than 20,000 followers. It is trying to encourage people to sign two petitions, one calling for a ban on the sale of plastic grass and another calling for an “ecological damage” tax on such lawns. They have gathered 7,276 and 11,282 signatures.
paras.zh: 皇家园艺学会的决定出台之际，活动人士正设法让更多人意识到人造草坪造成的问题。一个声称要“戳穿”人造草坪“绿色伪装”的推特账号已有两万多名关注者。它正鼓励人们签署两份请愿书，一份呼吁禁止销售塑料草坪，另一份呼吁对此类草坪征收“生态损害”税。两份请愿分别征集到 7,276 个和 11,282 个签名。

paras.en: However, supporters of fake grass point out that there is also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol. The industry also points out that real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments and that people who lay fake grass tend to use their garden more. The industry also claims that people who lay fake grass spend an average of £500 on trees or shrubs for their garden, which provides habitat for insects.
paras.zh: 然而，人造草坪的支持者指出，天然草坪同样会对环境造成影响——它需要修剪，因而通常要消耗电力或汽油。业界还指出，真草需要大量的水、除草剂或其他处理，而铺人造草坪的人往往更常使用自家花园。业界还称，铺人造草坪的人平均会花 500 英镑为花园购买树木或灌木，而这些植物为昆虫提供了栖息地。

paras.en: In response to another petition last year about banning fake lawns, which gathered 30,000 signatures, the government responded that it has “no plans to ban the use of artificial grass.”
paras.zh: 去年另一份要求禁止人造草坪的请愿书征集到 3 万个签名，对此政府回应称“没有禁止使用人造草坪的计划”。

paras.en: It added: “We prefer to help people and organizations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters. However, the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage, while measures such as the strengthened biodiversity duty should serve to encourage public authorities to consider sustainable alternatives.”
paras.zh: 政府还补充说：“我们更愿意帮助人们和组织做出正确的选择，而不是就此类事情立法。不过，人造草坪的使用必须遵守现行的法律与政策保障措施，以保护生物多样性并确保可持续的排水，而强化生物多样性义务等措施应有助于促使公共机构考虑可持续的替代方案。”

items.stem: The RHS thinks that plastic grass
opts: is a hot topic in gardening circles
is overpraised in the annual show
is ruining the view of west London
items.exp: 定位第一段末句：RHS introduced the ban because of the damage plastic grass does to the environment and biodiversity——禁令的理由就是“对环境有害”，故 A。B 借同段“反对的声音已传到园艺界最高层”设套，那是舆论传播的写法，不是 RHS 的看法；D 把“在伦敦西部办展”错接成“破坏伦敦西部景观”，地点巧合不等于观点。

items.stem: The petitions mentioned in Paragraph 3 reveal the campaigners'
items.exp: 定位第三段：两份请愿，一份 calling for a ban on the sale of plastic grass，另一份要征 “ecological damage” tax，矛头都对着人造草坪，故 B（反对使用人造草坪）。A 把请愿的对象误认成 RHS，其实请愿针对销售与税收；C 把“活动人士自己提议征税”读成“对征税愤怒”，主客颠倒；D 的“真草供应”全文未提。

items.stem: In Paragraph 4, supporters of fake grass point out
opts: the necessity to lower the costs of fake grass
the disadvantages of growing real grass
the way to take care of artificial lawns
the challenges of insect habitat protection
items.exp: 定位第四段：天然草坪 need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol，真草 requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments——列举的全是种真草的毛病，故 B。D 借段末“为昆虫提供栖息地”设套，可那是支持者反过来夸人造草坪的，不是“栖息地保护遇挑战”；A 的“降低成本”本段未涉及。

items.stem: What would the government do with regard to artificial grass?
opts: Urge legislation to restrict its use.
Take measures to guarantee its quality.
Remind its users to obey existing rules.
items.exp: 定位第五、六段：政府称 “no plans to ban”，又说 prefer to help people... rather than legislating，但强调 the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place——不另立新法，只要求使用者守现行规定，故 C。A 与 rather than legislating 直接冲突，是最强干扰；D 把“鼓励公共机构考虑可持续方案”放大成“替换人造草坪”；B 的“质量”无据。

items.stem: It can be learned from the text that fake grass
opts: has seen a market share decline
items.exp: 全文骨架就是争议：RHS 禁展、两份请愿、推特账号一边，支持者强调真草也耗电耗水、铺假草的人更爱打理花园另一边，政府又表态不禁——立场相反、各有依据，故 D。B 的“份额下降”无据，文中只说每年售出八百万平方米；A、C 的“不断改进”“越来越便宜”全文未涉及。

sections.title: Text 2　国家公园的资金缺口
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：国家公园缺钱，私有化不是解药。27 题 undercut 是“削弱”，别读成“支持”。

paras.en: It's easy to dismiss as absurd the federal government's ideas for plugging the chronic funding gap of our national parks. Can anyone really think it's a good idea to allow Amazon deliveries to your tent in Yosemite or food trucks to line up under the redwood trees at Sequoia National Park?
paras.zh: 联邦政府为填补国家公园长期资金缺口提出的种种设想，很容易被斥为荒唐。真有人觉得，让人把亚马逊的快递送到约塞米蒂的帐篷里，或者让餐车在红杉国家公园的红杉树下排成一列，是个好主意吗？

paras.en: But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis. Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion. Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling.
paras.zh: 但政府在一点上是对的：美国国家公园正处于危机之中。所有公园加起来的维修积压已超过 120 亿美元。道路、步道、洗手间、游客中心以及其他基础设施都在崩坏。

paras.en: But privatizing and commercializing the campgrounds would not be a cure-all. Campgrounds are a tiny portion of the overall infrastructure backlog, and businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues to the National Park Service.
paras.zh: 但把营地私有化、商业化并非万灵药。营地在全部基础设施积压中只占极小一部分，而且公园里的商家平均只把约 5% 的收入上缴给国家公园管理局。

paras.en: Moreover, increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat that overwhelms daily life.
paras.zh: 此外，进一步私有化肯定会削弱每年 3 亿游客来公园的主要理由之一：享受自然，暂时摆脱淹没日常生活的商业节奏。

paras.en: The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding. We conducted a comprehensive survey examining how U.S. residents view their national parks, and we found that Americans place a very high value on them—whether or not they actually visit them. The peer-reviewed economic survey of 700 U.S. taxpayers, conducted by mail and internet, also found that people would be willing to pay a significant amount of money to make sure the parks and their programs are kept intact. Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts to the national parks.
paras.zh: 真正的问题在于，公园长期缺乏资金。我们做了一项全面调查，考察美国居民如何看待国家公园，结果发现美国人非常看重国家公园——无论他们是否真的去过。这项经同行评议的经济调查覆盖 700 名美国纳税人，通过邮寄和网络进行，结果还发现，人们愿意支付相当数额的钱，以确保公园及其项目保持完好。约 81% 的受访者表示，他们愿意在未来 10 年多缴税，以避免国家公园遭到任何削减。

paras.en: The national parks provide great value to U.S. residents both as places to escape and as symbols of nature. On top of this, they produce value from their programs, their positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration, their contribution to our cultural and artistic life, and of course through tourism. The parks also help keep America's past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites—including Ellis Island and Gettysburg—and to bring the stories of these places to life.
paras.zh: 国家公园对美国居民极有价值，既是逃离日常的去处，也是自然的象征。除此之外，它们还通过自身项目、通过碳封存对气候的积极影响、对我们文化与艺术生活的贡献，当然还有通过旅游业，创造出价值。公园还帮助让美国的过去保持鲜活，它们与全国数千个地方辖区合作，保护历史遗址——包括埃利斯岛和葛底斯堡——并把发生在这些地方的故事讲活。

paras.en: The parks do all this on a shoestring. Congress allocates only $3 billion a year to the national park system—an amount that has been flat since 2001 (in inflation-adjusted dollars) with the exception of a one-time boost in 2009 as part of the Obama stimulus package. Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased by more than 50% since 1980, and now stands at 330 million visitors per year.
paras.zh: 公园做这一切都靠极少的钱。国会每年只向国家公园体系拨款 30 亿美元——按通胀调整后的美元计算，这一数字自 2001 年以来一直持平，只有 2009 年作为奥巴马刺激计划的一部分有过一次性增长。与此同时，年游客量自 1980 年以来增长了 50% 以上，如今达到每年 3.3 亿人次。

items.stem: What problem are U.S. national parks faced with?
items.exp: 定位第二段：they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion. Roads, trails, restrooms... are crumbling——维修积压与设施崩坏，即“基础设施维护不善”，故 D。A、B 都把第三段“私有化不是解药”反推成“园区商业化不够、商家利润下滑”，而文中说的是 privatization 会侵蚀游客体验；C 的“缺乏交通服务”文中无据。

items.stem: Increased privatization of the campgrounds may
items.exp: 定位第四段：increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come... to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat——私有化会冲掉游客“远离商业喧嚣”的体验，故 A。undercut 是“削弱”，B 的 help preserve nature 正好读反；C 的“运营压力”文中未提；D 与“游客来此是为了逃离商业化”逻辑相悖。

items.stem: According to Paragraph 5, most respondents in the survey would
opts: go to the national parks on a regular basis
advocate a bigger budget for the national parks
agree to pay extra for the national parks
support the national parks' recent reforms
items.exp: 定位第五段末句：Some 81% of respondents said they would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years to avoid any cuts——八成以上“愿意多缴税”，即 agree to pay extra，故 C。B 的“主张更大预算”把“自己多掏钱”换成“要求政府多拨款”，主体不同，是最强干扰；A 与 whether or not they actually visit them 相悖；D 的“近期改革”无据。

items.stem: The national parks are valuable in that they
opts: provide an income for the locals
items.exp: 定位第六段：The parks also help keep America's past alive... to protect historical sites—including Ellis Island and Gettysburg——保护历史遗址、讲活历史故事，即“具有历史意义”，故 B。A 把“通过旅游创造价值”夸大成“引领旅游业”；C 把 carbon sequestration 读成“资助气候研究”；D 的“为当地人提供收入”文中未提，属常识补足。

items.stem: It can be concluded from the text that the national park system
opts: is able to cope with staff shortages
is able to meet visitors' demands
is in need of a new pricing policy
is in need of a funding increase
items.exp: 定位末段：Congress allocates only $3 billion a year... has been flat since 2001，而游客量增长 50% 以上；前文更说 chronically starved of funding——结论是“需要增加资金”，故 D。A、B 与设施崩坏、维修积压正相反；C 的“新定价政策”把“缺钱”误读为“收费不合理”，全文未提门票价格。

sections.title: Text 3　互联网与人类记忆
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：上网改变的是“记什么”，不是“能否记”。32 题 cognitive offloading 落在“减轻负担”。

paras.en: The Internet may be changing merely what we remember, not our capacity to do so, suggests Columbia University psychology professor Betsy Sparrow. In 2011, Sparrow led a study in which participants were asked to record 40 factoids in a computer (“an ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain,” for example). Half of the participants were told the information would be erased, while the other half were told it would be saved. Guess what? The latter group made no effort to recall the information when quizzed on it later, because they knew they could find it on their computers. In the same study, a group was asked to remember both the information and the folders it was stored in. They didn't remember the information, but they remembered how to find the folders. In other words, human memory is not deteriorating but “adapting to new communications technology,” Sparrow says.
paras.zh: 哥伦比亚大学心理学教授贝齐·斯帕罗认为，互联网也许只是在改变我们记住的内容，而不是我们记忆的能力。2011 年，斯帕罗主持了一项研究，参与者被要求把 40 条冷知识（比如“鸵鸟的眼睛比它的大脑大”）录入电脑。一半参与者被告知信息会被删除，另一半则被告知信息会被保存。结果如何？后一组后来被测验时根本不去回想这些信息，因为他们知道自己可以在电脑上找到。同一项研究中，还有一组被要求既记住信息本身，也记住信息存在哪个文件夹。他们没记住信息，却记住了怎样找到文件夹。换句话说，斯帕罗说，人类的记忆并未退化，而是在“适应新的传播技术”。

paras.en: In a very practical way, the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as “cognitive offloading.” Traditionally, this role was fulfilled by data banks, libraries, and other humans. Your father may never remember birthdays because your mother does, for instance. Some worry that this is having a destructive effect on society, but Sparrow sees an upside. Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking—something that is not available on the Internet. “I personally have never seen all that much intellectual value in memorizing things,” Sparrow says, adding that we haven't lost our ability to do it.
paras.zh: 从很实际的意义上说，互联网正在成为我们记忆的外接硬盘，这一过程被称为“认知卸载”。传统上，这个角色由数据库、图书馆和其他人来承担。比如，你父亲可能从来记不住生日，因为你母亲记得。有人担心这会对社会产生破坏性影响，但斯帕罗看到了好的一面。她认为，这一趋势或许会把我们的学习方式从专注于零散事实与记忆，转向更侧重概念性思考——而这是互联网上得不到的。“我个人从不觉得背诵东西有多大智力价值，”斯帕罗说，并补充道我们并没有丧失这种能力。

paras.en: Still other experts say it's too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains. There is no experimental evidence showing that it interferes with our ability to focus, for instance, wrote psychologists Christopher Chabris and Daniel J. Simons. And surfing the web exercised the brain more than reading did among computer-savvy older adults in a 2008 study involving 24 participants at the Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior at the University of California, Los Angeles.
paras.zh: 还有别的专家说，现在就弄清互联网如何影响我们的大脑为时过早。例如，心理学家克里斯托弗·查布里斯和丹尼尔·J. 西蒙斯写道，没有实验证据表明它会干扰我们的专注能力。而在 2008 年一项涉及加州大学洛杉矶分校塞梅尔神经科学与人类行为研究所 24 名参与者的研究中，对电脑熟练的老年人上网浏览时大脑得到的锻炼比阅读时更多。

paras.en: “There may be costs associated with our increased reliance on the Internet, but I'd have to imagine that overall the benefits are going to outweigh those costs,” observes psychology professor Benjamin Storm. “It seems pretty clear that memory is changing, but is it changing for the better? At this point, we don't know.”
paras.zh: “我们对互联网依赖的加深可能带来代价，但我得说，总体而言好处会超过这些代价，”心理学教授本杰明·斯托姆评论道。“记忆显然正在改变，但它是往好的方向变吗？目前我们还不知道。”

items.stem: Sparrow's study shows that with the Internet, the human brain will
items.exp: 定位第一段实验：知道信息会被保存的一组 made no effort to recall the information，却记住了 how to find the folders——记忆的重心从“内容”转到“位置”，故 C（记忆重心的转移）。B 的“高效收集信息”把“不去记、只去检索”说成“收集”，方向相反，是最强干扰；D 的“延长记忆时长”与“只记路径”无关；A 的“细致分析”文中无据。

items.stem: The process of “cognitive offloading”
opts: enables us to classify trivial facts
items.exp: 定位第二段首句：the Internet is becoming an external hard drive for our memories, a process known as “cognitive offloading”——把记忆外包给“外接硬盘”，等于减轻记忆负担，故 D。B 的“使记忆不致失灵”过于绝对，原文只说记忆在 adapting，外接硬盘是替代而非修复，且后文还担心它对社会的破坏；A、C 的“识别假信息”“给琐碎事实分类”文中均无。

items.stem: Which of the following would Sparrow support about the Internet?
opts: It may reform our learning approach.
It may impact our society negatively.
It may enhance our adaptability to technology.
It may interfere with our conceptual thinking.
items.exp: 定位第二段：Perhaps, she suggests, the trend will change our approach to learning from a focus on individual facts and memorization to an emphasis on more conceptual thinking——她认为互联网会改变学习方式，故 A。B 与 but Sparrow sees an upside 相反；C 把“记忆在适应技术”偷换成“互联网提升我们的适应力”，主体错位；D 与“转向概念性思考”正好相反。

items.stem: It is indicated in Paragraph 3 that how the Internet affects our brains
opts: is most studied in older adults
is reflected in our reading speed
items.exp: 定位第三段首句：Still other experts say it's too soon to understand how the Internet affects our brains——“为时过早”，即仍需进一步研究，故 A。B 把“2008 年以老年人为对象的一项研究”扩大成“研究最多的是老年人”；C 的“阅读速度”与段中“上网比阅读更锻炼大脑”不是一回事；D 的“取决于上网习惯”文中未提。

items.stem: Neither Sparrow nor Storm would agree that
opts: our reliance on the Internet will be costly
the Internet is weakening our memory
memory exercise is a must for our brains
our ability to focus declines with age
items.exp: 定位第一段 human memory is not deteriorating but “adapting to new communications technology”，第四段斯托姆说记忆 is changing, but is it changing for the better? At this point, we don't know——一个明确否认退化，一个说好坏未知，都不认同“互联网在削弱记忆”，故 B。A 是斯托姆自己承认的（There may be costs），不能选；C 只有斯帕罗明确不认同，斯托姆未表态；D 两人都未涉及，属无据项。

sections.title: Text 4　青春期的矛盾
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：青少年为何既叛逆又乐于助人。38 题考“亲社会行为也在青春期达峰”，别只盯叛逆一面。

paras.en: Teenagers are paradoxical. That's a mild and detached way of saying something that parents often express with considerably stronger language. But the paradox is scientific as well as personal. In adolescence, helpless and dependent children who have relied on grown-ups for just about everything become independent people who can take care of themselves and help each other. At the same time, once cheerful and compliant children become rebellious teenage risk-takers.
paras.zh: 青少年是矛盾的存在。这是一种温和而超然的说法，父母们表达同一件事时用词往往要激烈得多。但这种矛盾既是个人层面的，也是科学层面的。在青春期，那些事事依赖大人的无助孩童，会变成能够照顾自己、也能互相帮助的独立个体。与此同时，曾经开朗听话的孩子，会变成叛逆的、爱冒险的少年。

paras.en: A new study published in the journal Child Development, by Eveline Crone of the University of Leiden and colleagues, suggests that the positive and negative sides of teenagers go hand in hand. The study is part of a new wave of thinking about adolescence. For a long time, scientists and policy makers concentrated on the idea that teenagers were a problem that needed to be solved. The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of opportunity as well as risk.
paras.zh: 发表在《儿童发展》期刊上的一项新研究由莱顿大学的埃弗琳·克罗内及其同事完成，它表明青少年积极与消极的两面是相伴而生的。这项研究属于一股关于青春期的新思潮。长期以来，科学家和政策制定者专注于这样一种看法：青少年是一个需要被解决的问题。而新研究强调，青春期既是风险的时期，也是机遇的时期。

paras.en: The researchers studied “prosocial” and rebellious traits in more than 200 children and young adults, ranging from 11 to 28 years old. The participants filled out questionnaires about how often they did things that were altruistic and positive, like sacrificing their own interests to help a friend, or rebellious and negative, like getting drunk or staying out late.
paras.zh: 研究者考察了 200 多名儿童和年轻成人身上的“亲社会”与叛逆特质，年龄从 11 岁到 28 岁。参与者填写问卷，回答自己多久做一次利他、积极的事，比如牺牲自己的利益去帮朋友，或者多久做一次叛逆、消极的事，比如喝醉或夜不归宿。

paras.en: Other studies have shown that rebellious behavior increases as you become a teenager and then fades away as you grow older. But the new study shows that, interestingly, the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior. Teenagers were more likely than younger children or adults to report that they did things like unselfishly help a friend.
paras.zh: 其他研究显示，叛逆行为在进入青春期时增多，随着年龄增长而消退。但新研究有趣地发现，同样的模式也适用于亲社会行为。相比年幼儿童或成年人，青少年更可能报告自己做过无私帮助朋友之类的事。

paras.en: Most significantly, there was a positive correlation between prosociality and rebelliousness. The teenagers who were more rebellious were also more likely to help others. The good and bad sides of adolescence seem to develop together.
paras.zh: 最重要的是，亲社会性与叛逆性之间存在正相关。越叛逆的青少年，也越可能去帮助别人。青春期好的与坏的一面似乎是共同发展的。

paras.en: Is there some common factor that underlies these apparently contradictory developments? One idea is that teenage behavior is related to what researchers call “reward sensitivity.” Decision-making always involves balancing rewards and risks, benefits and costs. “Reward sensitivity” measures how much reward it takes to outweigh risk.
paras.zh: 是否存在某种共同因素，构成了这些看似矛盾的发展的基础？一种看法是，青少年的行为与研究者所称的“奖赏敏感性”有关。决策总要权衡奖赏与风险、收益与代价。“奖赏敏感性”衡量的是需要多大的奖赏才能压过风险。

paras.en: Teenagers are particularly sensitive to social rewards—winning the game, impressing a new friend, getting that boy to notice you. Reward sensitivity, like prosocial behavior and risk-taking, seems to go up in adolescence and then down again as we age. Somehow, when you hit 30, the chance that something exciting and new will happen at that party just doesn't seem to outweigh the effort of getting up off the couch.
paras.zh: 青少年对社会性奖赏尤其敏感——赢下比赛、让新朋友印象深刻、让那个男孩注意到你。奖赏敏感性如同亲社会行为和冒险行为一样，似乎在青春期上升，随着我们变老又下降。不知怎的，等你到了 30 岁，那场聚会上会发生什么令人兴奋的新鲜事的可能性，似乎就是压不过从沙发上起身的那点力气了。

items.stem: According to Paragraph 1, children growing into adolescence tend to
opts: see the world in an unreasonable way
have fond memories of their past
items.exp: 定位第一段：helpless and dependent children... become independent people；同一段又说 once cheerful and compliant children become rebellious teenage risk-takers——同一批孩子身上长出两套相反的特质，故 A。B 把“矛盾”读成“看世界不讲道理”，是偷换概念；C、D 的“美好回忆”“对父母的感情”文中都没有出现，属凭空联想。

items.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 2 that Crone's study
opts: provides a new insight into adolescence
items.exp: 定位第二段：The study is part of a new wave of thinking about adolescence... The new work emphasizes that adolescence is a time of opportunity as well as risk——研究带来的是“对青春期的新认识”，故 C。D 的“突出青少年消极行为”正是被这项研究取代的旧思路；A、B 的“社会责任”“情绪问题”文中都没被列为研究内容。

items.stem: What does Crone's study find about prosocial behavior?
opts: It results from the wish to cooperate.
It is subject to family influence.
It tends to peak in adolescence.
items.exp: 定位第四段：the same pattern holds for prosocial behavior. Teenagers were more likely than younger children or adults to report that they did things like unselfishly help a friend——亲社会行为与叛逆行为同轨，青春期升、之后降，即“在青春期达到高峰”，故 D。A 的“源于合作意愿”、B 的“靠教育培养”、C 的“受家庭影响”文中都没有，其中 B 借“伦理教育”这类常识设套。

items.stem: It can be learned from the last two paragraphs that teenagers
opts: care a lot about social recognition
endeavor to live a joyful life
items.exp: 定位第六、七段：青少年对社会性奖赏特别敏感，所举 winning the game、impressing a new friend、getting that boy to notice you 全是“被看见、被认可”，故 B。A 把“想被别人注意”读成“高估自己对别人的影响”，主客颠倒，是最强干扰；C 的“对未来焦虑”与“追求奖赏”不是一回事；D 的“追求快乐生活”把 social rewards 泛化成享乐。

items.stem: What is the text mainly about?
items.exp: 全文主线：首段提出青少年“又独立又叛逆”的矛盾，第二至五段用克罗内的研究说明好坏两面同时发展，第六、七段用“奖赏敏感性”解释成因——通篇在回答“青少年为何自相矛盾”，故 A。B 只是解释机制之一，且文中关键词是 reward sensitivity 而非 risk-sensitive；C 只覆盖第四段一个发现；D 只对应首段半句话。

sections.title: Section II Part B　人名观点匹配
sections.dir: Read the following text and match each of the numbered items in the left column to its corresponding information in the right column. There are two extra choices in the right column. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 先划七项谓语再回文找人。C、E 分别出自文中没被点名的 Goodman 与 Rolande，最易误配。
subs: The rise of home prices is a temporary matter.
Builders possibly need to submit new estimates of their projects.
There will be specific limits on home extensions to prevent heat loss.
The new rules will take home prices to an even higher level.
Many people feel that home prices are already beyond what they can afford.
The new rules will affect people whose home extensions include new windows or doors.
The rule changes will benefit homeowners eventually.
sections.intro:
Net-zero rules set to send cost of new homes and extensions soaring

New building regulations aimed at improving energy efficiency are set to increase the price of new homes, as well as those of extensions and loft conversions on existing ones.

The rules, which came into effect on Wednesday in England, are part of government plans to reduce the UK's carbon emissions to net zero by 2050. They set new standards for ventilation, energy efficiency and heating, and state that new residential buildings must have charging points for electric vehicles.

The moves are the most significant change to building regulations in years, and industry experts say they will inevitably lead to higher prices at a time when a shortage of materials and high labour costs are already driving up bills.

blocks.en: Brian Berry, chief executive of the Federation of Master Builders, says the measures will require new materials, testing methods, products and systems to be installed. “All this comes at an increased cost during a time when prices are already sky high. Inevitably, consumers will have to pay more,” he says.
blocks.zh: 建筑大师联合会首席执行官布赖恩·贝里说，这些措施将要求安装新的材料、检测方法、产品和系统。“在价格本已高得离谱的时候，这一切都会带来更高的成本。消费者不可避免地要付更多的钱，”他说。
blocks.exp: 定位第四段贝里的话：All this comes at an increased cost... Inevitably, consumers will have to pay more——“成本上升、消费者多掏钱”，正是 D“新规把房价推到更高水平”。干扰项 C、E 看似也在讲房价与成本，但 C 是 42 块里古德曼的 25% 规定、E 是 43 块里罗兰德的抱怨，两人都不在 41–45 之列，属拿“同类声音”冒充贝里。

blocks.en: Gareth Belsham, of surveyors Naismiths, says people who are upgrading, or extending their home, will be directly affected. “The biggest changes relate to heating and insulation,” he explains. “There are new rules concerning the amount of glazing used in extensions, and any new windows or doors must be highly insulated.” Windows and doors will have to adhere to higher standards, while there are new limits on the amount of glazing you can have to reduce unwanted heat from the sun. Thomas Goodman, of MyJobQuote, says this will bring in new restrictions for extensions. “Glazing on windows, doors and roof lights must cover no more than 25% of the floor area to prevent heat loss,” he says.
blocks.zh: 测量师事务所 Naismiths 的加雷思·贝尔沙姆说，正在改造或扩建住宅的人将直接受到影响。“最大的变化与供暖和保温有关，”他解释说，“关于扩建部分使用多少玻璃，有了新规定，而且任何新门窗都必须高度隔热。”门窗必须达到更高的标准，同时对玻璃面积也有了新的上限，以减少太阳带来的多余热量。MyJobQuote 的托马斯·古德曼说，这将给扩建带来新的限制。“窗户、门和天窗的玻璃面积不得超过地面面积的 25%，以防热量流失，”他说。
blocks.exp: 定位第五段贝尔沙姆的话：people who are upgrading, or extending their home, will be directly affected，紧接着 new rules concerning the amount of glazing used in extensions, and any new windows or doors must be highly insulated——“扩建住宅、涉及新门窗的人会受直接影响”，故 F。C“以防热量流失的具体限制”出自本块后半的古德曼（25% 玻璃上限），他不是题号内人物，最易被误配。

blocks.en: As the rules came into effect last Wednesday, property developers were rushing to file plans just before the deadline. Any plans submitted before that date are considered to be under the previous rules, and can go ahead as long as work starts before 15 June next year. Builders which have costed projects, but have not filed the paperwork, may need to go back and submit fresh estimates, says Marcus Jefford of Build Aviator. Materials prices are already up 25% in the last two years. How much overall prices will increase as a result of the rule changes is not clear. “Whilst admirable in their intentions, they will add to the cost of housebuilding at a time when many already feel that they are priced out of homeownership,” says Jonathan Rolande of the National Association of Property Buyers. “An average extension will probably see around £3,000 additional cost thanks to the new regs.”
blocks.zh: 由于新规上周三生效，房地产开发商赶在截止日期前提交方案。凡在该日期之前提交的方案，都视为适用旧规，只要工程在明年 6 月 15 日之前开工即可继续推进。Build Aviator 的马库斯·杰福德说，已经算过造价但还没递交材料的建筑商，可能需要回头重新提交估价。过去两年材料价格已上涨 25%。新规会使总体价格上涨多少，目前还不清楚。“虽然他们的意图值得赞赏，但在许多人已经觉得自己被房价挤出局的时候，这还会推高建房成本，”全国房地产买家协会的乔纳森·罗兰德说。“拜新规所赐，一次普通扩建大概会多花 3,000 英镑左右。”
blocks.exp: 定位本块：Builders which have costed projects, but have not filed the paperwork, may need to go back and submit fresh estimates, says Marcus Jefford——算过价却没交材料的人要“重新提交估价”，与 B 的 possibly need to submit new estimates 同义，故 B。E“许多人觉得房价已超出承受能力”出自本块后半的罗兰德（priced out of homeownership），他不是题号内人物，是本题最强干扰。

blocks.en: John Kelly, a construction lawyer at Freeths law firm, believes prices will eventually come down. But not in the immediate future. “As the marketplace adapts to the new requirements, and the technologies that support them, the scaling up of these technologies will eventually bring costs down, but in the short term, we will all have to pay the price of the necessary transition.” he says.
blocks.zh: Freeths 律师事务所的建筑律师约翰·凯利认为，价格最终会降下来，但不会在近期。“随着市场适应新要求，以及支持这些要求的技术不断成熟，这些技术的规模化最终会降低成本，但短期内，我们都得为这一必要的过渡付出代价，”他说。
blocks.exp: 定位第十一段：凯利 believes prices will eventually come down. But not in the immediate future，又说 in the short term 大家先付代价、eventually 成本会降——涨价只是“暂时现象”，故 A。D“把房价推到更高水平”是贝里的判断，与凯利“最终回落”的方向正相反，是本块最强的干扰，只看“价格”一词就会误选。

blocks.en: However, the long-term effects of the changes will be more comfortable and energy-efficient homes, adds Andrew Mellor, of PRP architects. “Homeowners will probably recoup that cost over time in energy bill savings. It will obviously be very volatile at the moment, but they will have that benefit over time.”
blocks.zh: 不过，PRP 建筑事务所的安德鲁·梅勒补充说，这些变化的长期影响将是更舒适、更节能的住宅。“房主大概能随着时间推移，通过节省能源账单把钱收回来。眼下情况显然会很不稳定，但假以时日他们会得到这份好处。”
blocks.exp: 定位末段：长期影响是 more comfortable and energy-efficient homes，房主会 recoup that cost over time，并 will have that benefit over time——“最终让房主获益”，故 G。A 也提到“时间”，但说的是“涨价只是暂时”，主体是价格而非房主收益；C 的“防热量流失的限制”是古德曼的 25% 规定，与“长期获益”不是一回事。

sections.title: Section III　翻译
sections.dir: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 按句给分：先切主谓再调语序。them 指 reader，even when written 要译出“即便写下来”。

paras.en: In the late 18th century, William Wordsworth became famous for his poems about nature. And he was one of the founders of a movement called Romanticism, which celebrated the wonders of the natural world.
paras.zh: 18 世纪末，威廉·华兹华斯因其描写自然的诗作而声名鹊起。他还是“浪漫主义”运动的创始人之一，这一运动讴歌自然界的种种奇观。

paras.en: Poetry is powerful. Its energy and rhythm can capture a reader, transport them to another world and make them see things differently. Through carefully selected words and phrases, poems can be dramatic, funny, beautiful, moving and inspiring.
paras.zh: 诗歌是有力量的。它的能量与节奏能抓住读者，把读者带入另一个世界，让他们以不同的眼光看待事物。借助精心挑选的词句，诗歌可以是戏剧化的、诙谐的、优美的、动人的和鼓舞人心的。

paras.en: No one knows for sure when poetry began but it has been around for thousands of years, even before people could write. It was a way to tell stories and pass down history. It is closely related to song and even when written it is usually created to be performed out loud. Poems really come to life when they are recited. This can also help with understanding them too, because the rhythm and sounds of the words become clearer.
paras.zh: 没有人确切知道诗歌始于何时，但它已存在数千年，甚至在人类会书写之前就已出现。它是讲述故事、传承历史的一种方式。诗歌与歌曲关系密切，即便写成文字，通常也是为出声表演而创作的。诗歌只有在被朗诵时才真正活起来。这也有助于理解诗歌，因为词的节奏与读音变得更清晰了。

sections.title: Section IV Part A　应用文（建议信）
sections.dir: An art exhibition and a robot show are to be held on Sunday, and your friend David asks you which one he should go to. Write him an email to 1) make a suggestion, and 2) give your reason(s). Write your answer in about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name in your email. Use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
sections.note: 两个任务点：①明确推荐一个并给理由 ②提出具体安排。两边都说好就是没完成建议。
sections.sample:
Dear David,

I would suggest the art exhibition this Sunday. Here is why.

The robot show is entertaining, but most of what it displays can also be watched online, and the hall will be crowded with children. The exhibition, by contrast, is a rare chance to see more than a hundred original works from the Song dynasty, some of which have never left the museum. If we arrive early, we can also join the free guided tour at ten o'clock.

Shall we meet at the east gate at nine thirty? Just tell me if you would rather go to the other one, and I will come along happily.

Yours,
Li Ming
tips: 第一段一句话给出明确建议（选哪一个），不要写“两个都不错，看你喜欢”这种和事佬句子
第二段给两三条具体理由：一个讲机器人展“线上也能看、人多”，一个讲画展“真迹难得”，理由要落到事实上
第三段提出时间地点等具体安排，并留一句尊重对方选择的话，才像朋友之间的信
署名固定 Li Ming，不写真实姓名与地址；全文控制在 100 词左右，别写成议论文

sections.title: Section IV Part B　图表作文
sections.dir: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 图表：2012—2021 年我国居民健康素养水平，8.80%→25.40%，十年涨近两倍，2016 年后明显加速。
sections.sample:
The line chart shows the health literacy level of Chinese residents from 2012 to 2021. In 2012 only 8.80 percent of the population understood basic health information well enough to act on it; by 2021 the figure had reached 25.40 percent, almost three times the starting point. The rise was slow at first, gaining less than one percentage point a year, and then accelerated after 2016, when the rate passed 11 percent and began to climb by nearly three points a year.

Several factors explain the trend. Government campaigns have carried health knowledge into villages and communities, and the Internet has put reliable advice on almost every phone. People also have stronger reasons to care: as incomes rise, chronic diseases replace infectious ones as the main threat, and prevention depends on what citizens know.

The figures are encouraging, yet a quarter of the population is still far from enough. Health education should therefore remain a public priority, especially for older people in rural areas.
tips: 第一段只做“读数”：8.80% 升到 25.40%，点明“接近三倍”，再补一句“2016 年后加速”，比逐年报数有力
第二段归因分两层：供给端（政府宣传、互联网科普）+ 需求端（收入提高、慢病取代传染病）
这是百分数，别把 25.40 写成“25.40 亿/万”；引用数值保留两位小数更稳
结尾给一句方向性判断（四分之一仍不够、重点在农村老人），不要再开新话题
